sources.citation: Sadibekova et al. (2024), MCXC-II, A&A 688 A187; CDS J/A+A/688/A187, byte columns defined by https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/ftp/J/A+A/688/A187/ReadMe
Tully et al. (2023), Cosmicflows-4, ApJ 944, 94; CDS J/ApJ/944/94, tables 2 (group membership, 1PGC) and 3 (group distance modulus, DMzp), as joined into the Nearby Universe's tracked table

description: Seven nearby named galaxy clusters, independently selected from MCXC-II, each at the measured distance of its Cosmicflows-4 group (the group of its brightest galaxy). Centres and R500 apertures; Virgo and Fornax link to packages that draw their member galaxies.
distanceCaveat: Each centre is the MCXC-II X-ray position at its Cosmicflows-4 group's distance (the weighted average of the members' distance moduli, table 3 DMzp), where the Nearby Universe draws the members. The MCXC-II redshift's comoving distance (H0=70 km/s/Mpc, Omega_m=0.3) now only checks the catalogue's angular scale; it differs from the group distance by peculiar velocities, most for nearby Virgo and Fornax.
